Coordination

Event coordinators across Australia

Event coordination services for everything that is not a wedding. You build the plan, a coordinator confirms it, writes the run sheet and runs the event on the day.

What does an event coordinator do?

An event coordinator runs an event that somebody else has planned. They take the bookings, contracts and timings you already have, confirm every supplier, build one run sheet that everyone works from, and then manage the event on the day: bump in, set up, the schedule, the problems and the pack down.

Event coordination services and event planning are frequently sold by the same people, but they are not the same product and should not be priced the same. Planning is a months long build. Coordination is a short, intense handover followed by an on-site day. If a quote covers both, check that the scope actually reflects both.

Where it applies

When coordination is the right buy

01

Parties and private functions

You have booked the venue, the caterer and the band. What you have not solved is who tells the caterer the band needs to load in first. A coordinator solves that and hosts nothing.

Party planners
02

Corporate events

Conferences, awards nights, launches and staff events, where an internal team has built the programme and needs someone external to run the room on the day.

Corporate event planning
03

Weddings

Wedding coordination is a specialised version of the same job with its own timings, vocabulary and supplier set. It has its own page.

Wedding coordinators

The work

What is actually in an event coordination package

Handover and document review

The coordinator reads every contract, floor plan and timing you have, and comes back with the gaps. This is usually where the first real problems surface, which is the point.

Supplier confirmation

Every supplier is contacted and confirmed: arrival time, access route, power requirements, meal requirements, pack down window. Missing one of those is the classic cause of a bad bump in.

The run sheet

One document, one version, circulated to everyone. A run sheet that only exists in your head is not a run sheet.

Event run sheet guide

On-site management

The coordinator is the contact for suppliers, venue and staff for the whole event, so the host can be a host.

Your side

The brief a coordinator needs from you

A coordination handover is only as good as the material it starts with. Five things decide whether the first fortnight is productive or spent chasing paperwork.

01

Every supplier contract

Not a list of names. The signed contracts, so the coordinator can see what each supplier has actually committed to and what you have already paid for.

02

A contact for every supplier

The name and mobile of the person who will be on site, not the office number. This one detail prevents most bump in problems.

03

The venue's rules in writing

Access times, loading route, power, noise curfew, bump out deadline and any preferred supplier restrictions.

04

Your honest list of worries

The speech that will run long, the supplier who has gone quiet, the seating problem. The most useful thing you can hand over and the one most often left out.

Pricing

How event coordination is usually charged

Coordination is priced on the length of the handover and the hours on site, not on the size of your event budget.

Most Australian coordinators quote a flat fee for a defined package: a handover period, a set number of pre-event meetings, the run sheet, supplier confirmation, and a stated number of hours on site with a stated start and finish. Anything past the contracted finish is usually billed by the hour.

Published Australian figures for the wedding version of this work sit at roughly $1,500 to $2,000 according to Easy Weddings, in a guide updated February 2026, and $1,000 to $5,000 according to Airtasker, updated February 2025. Non-wedding coordination is generally quoted the same way, with the same three variables moving it: how long the handover runs, how many hours on site, and whether the event needs more than one coordinator on the ground.

When you compare two coordination quotes, compare the handover length and the on-site hours before the headline figure. A two week handover with eight hours on site is a materially smaller product than a six week handover with full-day cover, even when the two numbers look similar.

Longer programmes

Coordinating a multi-session or multi-day event

A conference, a festival or a two-day offsite is not a bigger party. The coordination work changes shape rather than just scale.

On a single-session event the coordinator manages one timeline. On a multi-session programme they are managing a schedule where every session has its own set-up, its own room configuration and often its own supplier, and where running fifteen minutes late in session two compounds through the rest of the day.

Three things become disproportionately important. The first is the changeover, meaning the window between one session ending and the next being ready, which is where multi-session events actually fail. The second is a single source of truth for the schedule, because internal stakeholders will otherwise circulate their own versions. The third is a named decision-maker on site who can approve a change without a phone call, since a coordinator who has to seek approval for every adjustment cannot keep a programme on time.

For multi-day events, add accommodation, catering across several services, and staff rostering that has to comply with break requirements. That is usually enough to move the job from coordination into full planning territory, and it should be quoted accordingly.

The other option

When you need a planner instead

You need a planner rather than a coordinator when the plan does not exist yet. The clearest test is the supplier list. If you can name every supplier and each one is booked, coordination is the right buy. If you are still choosing, you are asking a coordinator to do planning work that they have not quoted for and may not have the lead time to do.

The second test is the venue. If it is dry hire, meaning it supplies the room and little else, the volume of sourcing involved usually pushes the job into planning territory regardless of how organised you are. A packaged venue handling catering, staffing and furniture leaves far less to coordinate.

If you land between the two, partial planning exists for exactly that case. Our planning services page compares all three levels side by side.

Straight answers

Event coordinator questions

What is the difference between an event coordinator and an event planner?

An event planner builds the plan from a brief: concept, venue, suppliers, budget and timeline. An event coordinator takes a plan that already exists, confirms it and runs it on the day. If you have booked nothing, you want a planner. If most of it is booked, you want a coordinator.

How far out do I need to book an event coordinator?

Two to three months is typical, which allows a handover four to six weeks before the event. For a large corporate event with a complex programme, earlier is better because the coordinator often finds scheduling conflicts that take time to resolve.

Can a coordinator work with suppliers I chose?

Yes. That is the model. Coordination is built around suppliers you have already booked, and a coordinator should not be pushing you to change them at that stage unless something is genuinely wrong.

Do I need a coordinator if the venue has an events team?

A venue events team manages the venue. A coordinator manages your event, including the suppliers who are not part of the venue contract, the parts of the programme that happen elsewhere and the decisions nobody at the venue is authorised to make.
